![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14257924/assets/d3b5a9d779cddfb94e6bffc73c273dcc6df997259e09aed0c1b2db7c9529bc4e.png)

Consider the region $D$ shown above. If 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+{y}^{2}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

 
which of the following statements are true?

I. ${∬}_{D}(x+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,\,$ where $R=[-2,3]\times [-2,2]$

II. ${∬}_{R}(x+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,\,$ where $R=[-3,4]\times [-3,3]$

III. ${∬}_{D}(x+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A,\,$ where $R=[-2,4]\times [-3,3]$
question.worked_solution:
Notice that if $R$ covers $D$ completely and we define 

$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}x+{y}^{2}, & (x,y)\in R\cap D \\ 0, & (x,y)\in R∖D,\end{aligned}
$$

we obtain

$$
{∬}_{D}(x+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}A={∬}_{R}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine each of the given statements.

- Statement I is false. The rectangle $R$ does not cover the region $D.$

- Statement II is false. The integrals have not been stated correctly with respect to the domains $R$ and $D$ (they have been swapped).

- Statement III is true. The rectangle $R$ covers the region $D$ completely.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."
